summary: Abu Musa Ash'ari visits the ailing Hasan, and Ali confirms the Prophet's saying on the reward of visiting a sick Muslim brother.
notes: Two reports: a short version that refers back to 'as it appears above', then Abu Faakhita's fuller account.

summary: Umar asks to see Zaid while a slave girl is combing Zaid's hair, and Zaid comes to him; separately Abdullaah bin Mas'ood veils his wife when people ask to see him.
notes: Two separate reports: Zaid's account of Umar, and a second narration about Abdullaah bin Mas'ood.

summary: Musa bin Talha is struck by his father for entering without permission, and Hudhayfah warns a man who was peeping in before asking to enter.
notes: Two reports. The text says only 'Hudhayfah', matched to Hudhayfah bin Yamaan; please confirm, as several Hudhayfahs are in the vocabulary.

summary: Aa'isha and Uthmaan bin Abil Aas report that the Prophet loved the people of taqwa, and that he held Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Ammaar bin Yaasir dear until his death.
notes: Two reports: Aa'isha's saying and Uthmaan bin Abil Aas's saying.

summary: Amr bin Al Aas says he cannot tell whether the Prophet appointed him out of real affection or only to ease his heart, and names Abdullaah bin Mas'ood and Ammaar bin Yaasir as the two men the Prophet loved most.
notes: 'Hadhrat Hasan' is taken as Hasan al-Basri (not a Companion), who relays from Amr; please confirm.

summary: Amr bin Al Aas is told that Ammaar, whom the Prophet loved, was killed at Siffeen by their side, and he admits it.
notes: Continues the report at n01965 ('Another narration adds').

summary: Usaamah bin Zaid reports the Prophet naming Usaamah and then Ali as the family members he loved most, and Amr bin Al Aas reports the Prophet naming Aa'isha, Abu Bakr and Abu Ubaydah as the people he loved most.
notes: Two reports: Usaamah's account of Ali and Abbaas's visit, and Amr bin Al Aas's account of the questions about whom the Prophet loved.

summary: Anas reports that a Companion was told by the Prophet to tell a man he liked for Allaah's sake that he liked him, and that the man prayed for him in return.
Abdullaah bin Umar tells how, on the Prophet's instruction, he told a man he liked him for Allaah's sake.
Abdullaah bin Sarjas tells the Prophet he likes Abu Dharr, is told to tell him, does so, and the Prophet says that even mentioning it carries great reward.
notes: Abdullaah bin Sarjas is not in the vocabulary; the text gives (RA).

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that during a famine before the Prophet's mission, the Prophet and Abbaas took in Ali and Ja'far, while Abu Taalib kept Aqeel.
notes: Sulaymaan bin Dawood's closing remark about Ja'far is a second narrator.

summary: Jaabir reports that when Juwayriyyah wanted to free one of her slaves, the Prophet advised giving the slave to an uncle among the Bedouin instead, for a greater reward.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence ('This will earn you a greater').

summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that when the verse on giving the relative his due was revealed, the Prophet told Faatima she could have his land at Fidak.
notes: The Qur'anic verse is garbled by OCR, so its exact wording is not reliable here.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports a man who complained that his relatives cut ties with him, and the Prophet told him that an angel stays with him as long as he keeps treating them well.
Abdullaah bin Amr reports a man who complained that his relatives cut ties with him, and the Prophet told him to take the better course and keep up the bonds of kinship.
Abu Hurayrah warns that the deeds of anyone who severs family ties are not accepted, and a young man who had been estranged from his aunt for two years goes to ask him why.
notes: Abu Ayyoob Sulaymaan is not in the vocabulary and the text does not give (RA).

summary: A'mash reports that Abdullaah bin Mas'ood asked those who sever family ties to leave a gathering before he made du'aa, since the doors of heaven are closed to them.
Khaarijah bin Zaid reports that Zaid bin Thaabit described how the Prophet joined in every kind of conversation with his companions, whether about worldly matters, the Aakhirah or food.

Safiyya bint Huyay says she never saw anyone with better character than the Prophet, recalling how he gently woke her on the journey back from Khaybar and later explained what he had been forced to do to the Jews of Khaybar.
notes: A citation to Abu Nu'aym's Dalaa'il (Pg.57) sits inside the text. It is a reference, so it is not tagged as a person.

summary: Another narration says that even the slave girls of Madinah could take the Prophet by the hand and lead him wherever they needed him to go.
notes: Very short, and no narrator is named in the text (the heading names Abu Hurayrah and Anas).

summary: Anas reports that a woman with a mental illness asked the Prophet for help, and he stepped aside with her into a street to hear her problem.
Muhammad bin Maslamah says that when he returned from a journey, the Prophet took him by the hand and did not let go until he did.
Aa'isha says the Prophet always chose the easier of two options when it involved no sin, and that he took revenge only for the sake of Allaah.
Aa'isha reports that the Prophet never struck a servant or a woman, always took the easier option when it involved no sin, and punished only when Allaah's prohibitions were violated.
notes: Two separate Aa'isha reports joined in one item.

summary: Hasan reports that the Prophet said he could find fault with each of his Companions' characters except Abu Ubaydah's.
notes: 'Hasan' is taken as Hasan al-Basri (not a Companion), as the report is given without a Companion's link; please confirm.

summary: A narrator whose name is garbled in the text reports that the Prophet, visiting his daughter as she washed Uthmaan's head, told her to treat Uthmaan well because his character was closest to his own.
notes: The narrator's name is garbled by OCR, so no narrator is tagged. The daughter is Ruqayya per the next narration.

summary: Abu Hurayrah reports that Ruqayya, combing the Prophet's hair, said he had just asked how Uthmaan was, and then praised Uthmaan's character as closest to his own.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence ('closest to my').

summary: Abdullaah bin Aslam reports that the Prophet told Ja'far he resembled him in looks and in character.
notes: Abdullaah bin Aslam is not in the vocabulary; the text gives (RA).

summary: Ali, Usaamah bin Zaid and Abdullaah bin Ja'far report the Prophet's words to Ja'far, Zaid and Ali, and Abdullaah says he would not trade them for red camels.
notes: Several reports joined, and cut off at the end ('your father (Ja'far'). 'Zaid' is taken as Zaid bin Harithah, the Prophet's freed slave; please confirm.

summary: Aamir bin Rabee'ah says Mus'ab bin Umayr was his close friend from the time Mus'ab accepted Islaam until his martyrdom at Uhud, and that he never saw a better character.
Habba Urani reports that people praised Abdullaah bin Mas'ood in front of Ali, and Ali called on Allaah to witness that he agreed with their praise.
notes: Two reports: Habba's account and an additional narration of further praise.

summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that Dhu Khuwaysarah demanded justice from the Prophet, that Umar asked to behead him, and that the Prophet forbade it while describing the people who would come from him.
notes: The second paragraph is Abu Sa'eed's further testimony about Ali's search for the man, from the same narrator.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar reports that when Abdullaah bin Ubay died, his son asked the Prophet for a shirt to shroud him and for the funeral prayer, and the Prophet prayed before the verse forbidding it was revealed.
Aa'isha says that when news reached the Prophet of something someone had said, he never named that person, but spoke of people in general.
Aa'isha says she never saw the private parts of the Prophet.
notes: Ends with a stray section heading ('The Modesty of the Sahabah (RA)') that is not part of the narration.

summary: Sa'eed bin Al Aas reports that the Prophet let Abu Bakr and Umar in as he lay covered, but sat up and covered himself for the bashful Uthmaan, and explains why when Aa'isha asks.
notes: The second paragraph is Aa'isha's question, continuing the same report.

summary: Sulaym bin Abu Hudhayl says that when Jareer bin Abdullaah left his house and mounted his mule, he took his slave up behind him.
Abdullaah bin Salaam carries a bundle of wood through the marketplace to guard against pride, quoting the Prophet that someone with even an atom of pride will not enter Jannah.
Ali says the core of humility is to greet others first, to accept a lower place in a gathering, and to dislike ostentation and boasting.
Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee reports that during the Tabook expedition he jokingly asked the Prophet 'All of me?' when he was let into a very small tent, and Waleed explains the joke.

people.name: Waleed bin Uthmaan bin Abu Aaliyah

notes: Waleed's closing line explains the joke; it is an explanatory aside rather than a separate report.
